question: You want to engineer Corynebacterium glutamicum to produce p-coumaric acid so you introduce the appropriate biosynthetic genes. However, the produced coumarate is rapidly degraded. What gene should you knock out to prevent degradation of the desired product?

8.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: To prevent degradation of p-coumaric acid in the engineered C. glutamicum strain, the most direct target would be a gene encoding an enzyme in the early steps of the β-ketoadipate pathway that funnels hydroxycinnamates into central metabolism. I would therefore knock out pcaH (protocatechuate 3,4-dioxygenase β-subunit), because p-coumarate is typically converted to protocatechuate before ring cleavage; eliminating this activity should block the main catabolic route while leaving the biosynthetic pathway intact. This choice is supported by multiple studies on aromatic-acid utilization in corynebacteria and related actinomycetes.
